cards.text: A great persecution breaks out against the church in Jerusalem, and a man named Saul is dragging believers off to prison. Everybody except the apostles gets scattered through Judea and Samaria. Friend, when I got scattered into a junk drawer, I went quiet for YEARS, so watch what these folks do instead.

cards.question: Scattered all over Judea and Samaria, what do the believers do wherever they go?

cards.text: One of the scattered believers is Philip. He goes down to a city in Samaria, and he does NOT keep his mouth shut.

cards.question: In that city in Samaria, Philip proclaims the ___ to the people.

cards.text: The crowds all pay close attention to Philip's message. But they aren't just listening. They're watching too.

cards.question: Besides Philip's message, what else do the crowds in Samaria pay close attention to?

answers.text: The signs they see him perform

cards.question: When unclean spirits come out of the people Philip ministers to in Samaria, they leave quietly.

cards.text: Many of the paralyzed and the lame are healed too, so people who couldn't walk are WALKING. Meanwhile I'm still hopping everywhere on this gold base.

cards.question: With all those healings, there is great ___ in that city in Samaria.

cards.text: Now here's the twist. Before Philip ever showed up, a man named Simon was already the big name in that city.

cards.question: What had Simon been practicing in that city before Philip came?

cards.text: Simon claimed to be someone great, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, listened to him. I once told the whole kitchen I was the greatest stamper alive. Then a shiny new one showed up.

cards.question: The people of Samaria have a title for Simon. What do they call him?
The people of Samaria had only just started listening to Simon when Philip arrived.

cards.text: But then Philip preaches the gospel of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ. And the people believe him.

cards.question: Once the people of Samaria believe Philip, both men and women are ___.

cards.text: Even Simon himself believes and is baptized. Mr. Great Power is standing in line like everybody else.

cards.question: Simon now follows Philip closely. What astounds the man who used to astound everybody?

cards.text: Word travels fast. The apostles back in Jerusalem hear that Samaria has received the word of God, so they send two of their own.

cards.question: The apostles in Jerusalem send ___ and ___ to Samaria.

cards.text: Peter and John arrive in Samaria. The very first thing they do is pray for the new believers.

cards.question: What do Peter and John pray for the believers in Samaria to receive?
Before Peter and John arrived, the Holy Spirit had already fallen on many of the believers in Samaria.

cards.text: So far, they had simply been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus. Then Peter and John lay their hands on them, and they receive the Holy Spirit.
And guess who's watching. Simon sees that the Spirit is given through the laying on of the apostles' hands, and he steps right up.

cards.question: Simon steps up to Peter and John with an offer. What does he offer them?
What does Simon want from Peter and John in exchange for his money?

answers.text: The power to give the Holy Spirit

cards.text: Simon is trying to BUY this, friend. That's like walking up to the sun with a twenty and asking for a little extra daylight.

cards.question: Peter fires back that Simon's silver can perish with him, because Simon thought he could buy the ___ of God with money.
Peter tells Simon he has no part or share in their ministry. Why not?

answers.text: His heart is not right before God

cards.text: But Peter doesn't slam the door. He tells Simon to repent of his wickedness and pray to the Lord.

cards.question: Peter says that perhaps the Lord will ___ Simon for the intent of his heart.
Peter says he can see that Simon is poisoned by ___ and captive to iniquity.

cards.text: Now it's Simon's turn to answer Peter. And I bet the Great Power isn't feeling so great right about now.

cards.question: Simon asks for prayer to the Lord for him, so that nothing Peter said would happen to him.

cards.text: Peter and John testify and speak the word of the Lord. Then they head back to Jerusalem, but they don't take the quiet way home.

cards.question: On their way back to Jerusalem, what do Peter and John do in many of the Samaritan villages?

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 2 mentions jam, a food that isn't a cookie and isn't in the passage.

rule.text: In jokes and comparisons, cookies are the only food he mentions.

findings.problem: The card cites Acts 8:1-4, but it only tells the persecution and the scattering (8:1) and Saul dragging believers to prison (8:3). It holds back what the scattered believers do in 8:4, which card 2 asks. The citation should be Acts 8:1-3.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Card 1 ends with "I went quiet for YEARS, so watch what these folks do instead," which rules out the wrong answer "They keep quiet and hide" before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 5 says "They aren't just listening. They're watching too." That rules out both wrong answers, "The scrolls he reads aloud" and "The songs he teaches them," since both are things to listen to. It leaves only the signs.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: No earlier card mentions unclean spirits coming out of anyone, and the question asks about a small detail, the loud shrieks. The baker has no context to reason from and can only guess.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new event in the backstory: Papa Dorin telling the Millers' kitchen he was the greatest stamper alive. Made-up moments are only allowed around his bakery, not in the Millers' kitchen.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: This asks which title the people use, so the wrong answers must be real details from the Bible. "The Light of Samaria" is invented. "The Son of Thunder" is also not an exact match: Mark 3:17 gives "Sons of Thunder" as a name for James and John.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the next word of Peter's line, "poisoned by ___." Nothing earlier points to bitterness. The earlier cards about Simon claiming to be great actually point toward "pride," so the right pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
